children: Ahead of policy decisions in the US, UK and Japan, traders are now pricing in three to four rises in a year. It looks excessive: the energy price spike is more likely to sap growth than fuel lasting inflation. Unless officials push back, market views may become self-fulfilling.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Jon Sindreu on X and LinkedIn.

The Federal Reserve will announce its latest monetary policy decision on September 16. As of 0830 GMT, derivatives markets pointed to a 93% chance that officials would raise the federal funds target range by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.75%-4.00%, according to CME FedWatch.
The Bank of England and the Bank of Japan are scheduled to hold policy meetings on September 17 and September 18, respectively.
